title: Finger Heart Emoji 🫰 Meaning: Korean Heart or Money?
description: 🫰 is the Korean finger heart: thumb and index finger crossed to make a tiny heart. It also reads as a money or snapping gesture. Learn which one is meant.
summary: 🫰 shows a hand with the thumb and index finger crossed. Its main meaning is the finger heart, a small sign of love and thanks popularized in South Korea and spread worldwide by K-pop. Because the pose also resembles rubbing fingers together or snapping, some people use it for money or “just like that.”
meaning: Cross the tip of your thumb over the tip of your index finger and the two form a miniature heart. That gesture, known as the finger heart, became a signature of South Korean celebrities and K-pop idols during the 2010s and travelled with their fandoms. 🫰 is the emoji for it, and among people familiar with Korean pop culture it simply means “love you” or “thank you,” delivered in a cute, compact way.

Outside that context the picture is easy to read differently. Rubbing a thumb against the fingers is a widespread gesture for cash, so 🫰 gets used for “that’s expensive,” “pay me,” or “money talks.” Unicode’s own keywords for the emoji include both “love” and “money,” which reflects how split the usage really is. A third reading is the finger snap: “done, just like that 🫰.”

Which meaning lands depends on your audience. In fan communities, comment sections for Korean artists and dramas, and among younger users generally, the heart reading dominates. In finance jokes, shopping talk and messages about prices, the money reading takes over. If you are unsure how it will be received, pairing it with ❤️ or 💸 removes any doubt about what your crossed fingers are saying.

The emoji was added in Emoji 14.0 in 2021 under the descriptive name “Hand with Index Finger and Thumb Crossed,” wording that stays deliberately neutral about what the gesture signifies. It supports skin tones, and many people use it as a lighter, more playful alternative to a full heart: small enough for a casual thank-you, sweet enough to end a goodnight text.

contexts.label: In K-pop and fan spaces
contexts.body: Here 🫰 is unambiguous. Fans flood comments with it to send love to idols, and it mirrors what artists do on stage, in photo shoots and at fan signings. It often appears with purple, pink or white hearts and with a group’s fandom emoji. Using it marks you as someone who knows the gesture, which is part of its appeal.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Among friends it works as a quick “love ya” or “thanks” that feels less serious than ❤️. It is common at the end of a goodnight message or after a small favor. If the person you are texting does not follow Korean pop culture, expect an occasional “why are you snapping at me?”

contexts.label: Talking about money
contexts.body: People send 🫰 when a price is steep, when payday arrives, or when hinting that something will cost you. “Rent is due 🫰” and “that bag is 🫰🫰🫰” both use the fingers-rubbing sense. Small businesses and resellers use it in captions about deals and payments for the same reason. In this sense it has nothing to do with affection.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: A finger heart from someone you like is flirty but gentle. It is affectionate without the intensity of a red heart, so people use it when they are testing the waters. It is also popular between friends, so a single 🫰 is encouraging rather than conclusive. Watch whether hearts or more direct compliments follow.

examples.text: Thanks for the notes, you saved me 🫰
examples.meaning: A light, affectionate thank-you using the finger heart.
Excited fan love, in the style of K-pop fandom posts.

examples.text: That jacket is cute but the price 🫰🫰
examples.meaning: The jacket is expensive; the gesture stands for money.
A small, sweet sign of affection at the end of a chat.

examples.text: Fixed the bug in two minutes 🫰
examples.meaning: A finger snap: it was done instantly and easily.
Looking forward to money coming in.

combos.meaning: Makes the finger heart meaning explicit: sending love.
Money being spent, or something costing a lot.
A cute, sparkly thank-you or a snap that makes something happen like magic.
Doubling up on hand hearts for extra affection.

confusedWith.difference: 🫶 forms a large heart with both hands and only ever means love, thanks or support. 🫰 is a one-handed mini heart that can also be read as a money or snapping gesture.
🤏 holds the thumb and index finger slightly apart to show a small amount or size. In 🫰 the two fingers cross over each other, which is what creates the heart shape.
👌 joins thumb and index finger into a circle with the other fingers raised, meaning “perfect” or “OK.” 🫰 keeps the other fingers folded and crosses the fingertips instead of forming a ring.

avoid: Do not rely on it for affection with people unfamiliar with the finger heart, who may see a snap or a demand for money.
Avoid it in messages about debts or payments at work, where rubbing fingers for cash can look crass.
Skip it in formal thanks, where a written sentence does the job more clearly.
design: The emoji shows a single hand, usually seen from the back or side, with the remaining fingers curled into the palm and the thumb crossed over the index fingertip. On most platforms the crossed tips sit at the top so they suggest a tiny heart. Angle and hand orientation vary between vendors, which is one reason the same emoji can look more like a snap in one place and a heart in another.

faqs.q: Is 🫰 a heart or a money sign?
faqs.a: Both readings are real. It was designed with the Korean finger heart in mind and is most often used for love and thanks, but the pose matches the fingers-rubbing gesture for cash, so plenty of people use it for money or high prices. Surrounding words and emojis tell you which.

faqs.q: What does 🫰 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: Usually affection in a playful, low-key form: a small “love you,” “you’re sweet,” or “thanks.” If they like K-pop or Korean dramas, it is almost certainly a finger heart. Friends send it as freely as crushes do, so it is not proof of romantic interest.

faqs.q: Where does the finger heart come from?
faqs.a: The gesture took off in South Korea, where actors, singers and idols made it a standard pose for photos and fan interactions in the 2010s. Global interest in K-pop and Korean television carried it abroad, and it is now common among fans of all kinds.

Some people use it that way, for “in a snap” or “just like that,” because the hand looks ready to snap. There is no separate finger-snapping emoji, so 🫰 fills the gap, although that is not the meaning it was named for.

faqs.q: When was 🫰 added to emoji keyboards?
faqs.a: It was approved in Emoji 14.0 in 2021, in the same batch as heart hands 🫶 and the index finger pointing at the viewer 🫵. Older devices that have not been updated may show a blank box instead.
